main:
[[people]] don’t understand words –
you have to communicate phonetically
for example: [[i]] woke up
and saw [[rain]] outside the window
dripdripdripdripdripdripdrip
you can look out the window phonetically
too, especially at the weather
dripdripdripdripdripdripdripdripdrip
crying? you can communicate
nonverbally too
let me kiss [[you]] on the forehead now
like at /someone’s/ funeral
we know it’s best to hold them
in an overcast summer
1:
tiredness – a gray word reeking of smoke
a word smoked like meat. not very pleasant.
of course, i can tell you how i follow my friends’ example
do yoga every morning and eat bitter food
go interesting places on money i make at a job i love
and plan to have a girl by 35
call her li or za and will i call her?
you know there’s only truth in poems
i really can do that and i can do all sorts of things
2:
when with a tired gesture
you draw out with dry fingers
your wrinkled cigarette
turn it in your hands so habitually
to the chatter of moscow crows
and the barking of foreign objects
when you climb up feet and all
onto the windowsill, pressing yourself tremulously
to the double glazing you know by heart
for the hundredth time
billions of years later
then you realize, wrinkling
the cracks in your calloused lips:
all that was childhood
like a smack on the ass at five
from your father or like new year’s
it was all childhood:
your first sex and your last word
voices doling out stinging slaps
village pool, strawberries on sale
first cigarettes, cider with that sweet
girl on her old balcony
you realize suddenly that it’s
a fair way from the real you.
that longing eats away at you because
you’re forgetting what it was like to smoke
your first cigarette
you don’t remember how to get up off this windowsill
without crying an old woman’s tears
looking into the mirror of the eyes of dead youth
and that tiny plasticine
«recently»
3:
my sweet lizzie
tonight the stars are like in david lynch films
abstinence gives birth to a dance inside
be patient and build up fluid
hit the brake on the turn
and pull into oncoming traffic
but that’s beside what i meant to tell you
digging your nails into the spirit of meiji
or in the waste left over from carax
locking onto the earth one last time
love the whole world and me
i’ll cover you with a blanket, and you’ll argue
about which trams ran when we were seventeen or so
4:
we sit facing each other
glass pours outside the window
same as ever
we were remembering our comrade again
the dead don’t die, the young – even less so
and you already smoke hash every day
and you’re surprised i’m already almost married
and we’re both afraid of perishing
and we’re both waiting so hard for the end
and to think we sat down facing each other
when we were fifteen
5:
living is actually very simple it just hurts basically like standing on nails
but if you stand on nails to songs by aquarium it’s kind of all right
and if you paint your nails at the same time it’s actually almost great
if you add sex and photos of anna karina you can even feel pleasure
only then it gets hard to hold it all together standing on nails
6:
showing off your sores and your sparkly bits
when you’re having tea and he says
yes, suicide – a good way out
in this situation we’ve gotten into
it doesn’t matter how fast
we’re tearing down the freeway to «i»
while you play princess
we’re too un-fashionable
and while i spoon out
the blue from your skull
cat and mouse, we look at the stars
catch tears on our tongues instead of snow
while you draw little circles in your notebook
heave-ho, lower away, playing god so absurdly
and shout «we need to be more serious»
giving me sweets like i’m a little child
teenagers in teslas hurtle past us
to songs that by nineteen
they’ll say oh where did my youth go
my barefoot old age –
the point of balance between knowing
i’ll definitely come to an end
and knowing
childhood has come for you and me
in striped socks
7:
everyone knows the achilles heel is the main character’s weak spot
once it’s wounded the hero dies
nobody says how much it hurts the hero
when they prick him in the right heel
mine stings so much i want to howl
otherwise i think i’m okay
8:
i’ve got a screeching nail-yanking apparatus of my very own
it’s still little, but soon it’ll grow up and start stealing fish
paying bribes and taking out mortgages
it sits in my right lung and scrapes the epithelium while i smoke my fifth marlboro in a row, chasing the cigarette
with cucumbers
the money’s running out, so’s my phone battery - no adapter
but the east of moscow won’t run out
because it’s all inside
9:
i live inside the motion picture assa –
i dance too much, love guys in suits
and dream of banananas on sale
you wouldn’t think i’m about to kill somebody
